Total number of questions — 20
37
State Government proposals for
development of science and
technology
*121. SHRI NATUJI HALAJI
THAKOR: Will the Minister of SCIENCE
AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether various State Governments
including Bihar and Gujarat have sent their
proposals to the Central Government for
development of science and technology in
the States during the last three years and
the current year;
(b) if so, the details thereof, year-wise
and State-wise;
(c) the details of the proposals
approved/rejected by Government during
the said period, State-wise;
(d) the details of the proposals lying
pending and the reasons therefor; and
(e) by when the pending proposals are
likely to be cleared?
Extraction of minerals by private
companies
*122. SHRI D. RAJA: Will the Minister
of MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that various
private sector companies, which were
allocated mining blocks, were extracting
more iron and manganese ores than the
permissible limit set by the authorities;
(b) if so, the details thereof along with a
list of such companies and the quality of
excess ores extracted by them during the
last three years, ore-wise;
(c) whether Government has made any
assessment regarding the loss to the public
exchequer due to such extractions;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the details of the action taken against
those companies and the steps taken to
recover the losses ?

38
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Funding of political parties
*123. DR. JANARDHAN
W AGHMARE: Will the Minister of LAW
AND JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has framed a
new law to make funding of political parties
more transparent;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the influence of black
money in elections has increased during the
last few years; and
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government
to check the same?
Development of rural areas
†*124. SHRI ISHWARLAL
SHANKARLAL JAIN: Will the Minister
of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that development
of the country, particularly of rural areas,
is far too less and development of villages
in comparison to cities is almost nil;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government proposes to
develop rural areas by earmarking special
packages therefor;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Flexi-fund for rural development
programmes
*125. SHRI NAND KUMAR SAI: Will
the Minister of RURAL DEVELOP-
MENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
set up a flexi-fund for various rural
development programmes designed by the
States, according to their needs;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) the details of the criteria fixed for
allocation of flexi-fund to various States;
(d) the details of the guidelines issued
to various States for utilization of the fund;
and
(e) the details of the steps taken by the
Central Government to ensure proper
utilization of the fund by various States?
Production of coal
*126. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: W ill the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the productivity of coal sector
during the last three years;
(b) whether any increase in coal
production has been witnessed after
allowing private sector in this sector; and
(c) the ratio of production of coal by
Coal India Ltd. and the private sector?
Solar and wind energy
*127. SHRI AAY ANUR
MANJUNATHA: Will the Minister of
NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has formulated
any plans for use of solar and wind energy
in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the extent to which solar and wind
energy is likely to fill up the gap between
demand and supply of power during the
next five years?

39
Safe drinking water in rural areas
*128. SHRIMATI KUSUM RAI: Will
the Minister of DRINKING WA TER AND
SANITA TION be pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of households in rural
areas which are lacking facilities of safe and
potable water in the country, State-wise;
(b) the percentage of households which
are presently consuming drinking water
having heavy metals more than the
permissible limits of WHO, State-wise;
(c) whether Government would frame a
national policy to provide safe and potable
water to the rural population, in view of
the shortage of safe and potable water in
most parts of the country;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
